# Chelsea feature five times - Top ten Premier League record transfer spends in one window

![Image 19: Chelsea feature five times - Premier League record transfer spends in one window](https://img.a.transfermarkt.technology/foto/galerie/spend-spot-1725626713-147376.png?lm=4711)

©TM/IMAGO

The transfer window closed for [English Premier League](https://www.transfermarkt.us/premier-league/startseite/wettbewerb/GB1 "Premier League") clubs and, once again, they outspent any other league in the world - by some distance. Premier League clubs €2.33 billion on new players with star names like [Leny Yoro](https://www.transfermarkt.us/leny-yoro/profil/spieler/923831 "Leny Yoro"), [João Félix](https://www.transfermarkt.us/jo-o-f-lix/profil/spieler/462250 "João Félix") and [Riccardo Calafiori](https://www.transfermarkt.us/riccardo-calafiori/profil/spieler/502821 "Riccardo Calafiori") moving to the English top-light.

  
  

[Premier League clubs, however, also broke the all-time record for highest transfer income by any league in history with €1.62 bn recouped from player sales](https://www.transfermarkt.us/-euro-1-62bn-in-player-sales-premier-league-breaks-transfer-income-record/view/news/443392). [Manchester City](https://www.transfermarkt.us/manchester-city/startseite/verein/281 "Manchester City") made the highest transfer profit in the Premier League, while Brighton had the biggest net spend of any team in the world! [Chelsea](https://www.transfermarkt.us/chelsea-fc/startseite/verein/631 "Chelsea FC") were the biggest spenders again with €239m paid out on new arrivals. But where does this rank in terms of the highest total transfer fees paid by a Premier League club in one window? Let’s find out.

  

## The Premier League’s biggest spenders in one transfer window

  

Chelsea’s total spend of €239m this summer would only rank 9th for biggest outlays in one window in Premier League history. The Stamford Bridge club are constantly scrutinized for their spending but they also €198m in sales and their net spend of €40.5m was just the 24th highest in the word. Chelsea, however, have spent the three largest amounts in one window in Premier League history and they’ve all arrived since BlueCo - fronted by Todd Boehly - gained ownership.

  

![Image 20](https://tmssl.akamaized.net//images/foto/newsansicht/big-spenders-1725626740-147377.png?lm=1725626747)As the graphic above illustrates, Chelsea’s €464m spend in the summer of 2023 is a record for English clubs with [Moisés Caicedo's](https://www.transfermarkt.us/mois-s-caicedo/profil/spieler/687626 "Moisés Caicedo") €116m arrival from Brighton a club record. The only winter window that features in the top ten belongs to Chelsea in January 2023 when they spent €330m on the likes of [Enzo Fernandez](https://www.transfermarkt.us/enzo-fern-ndez/profil/spieler/648195 "Enzo Fernández") and [Mykhaylo Mudryk](https://www.transfermarkt.us/mykhaylo-mudryk/profil/spieler/537860 "Mykhaylo Mudryk"). Chelsea feature five times in the top ten with Manchester City twice and [Manchester United](https://www.transfermarkt.us/manchester-united/startseite/verein/985 "Manchester United"), [Arsenal](https://www.transfermarkt.us/arsenal-fc/startseite/verein/11 "Arsenal FC") and [Tottenham](https://www.transfermarkt.us/tottenham-hotspur/startseite/verein/148 "Tottenham Hotspur") are in once.

# Chelsea feature five times - Top ten Premier League record transfer spends in one window

![Image 19: Chelsea feature five times - Premier League record transfer spends in one window](https://img.a.transfermarkt.technology/foto/galerie/spend-spot-1725626713-147376.png?lm=4711)

©TM/IMAGO

The transfer window closed for [English Premier League](https://www.transfermarkt.us/premier-league/startseite/wettbewerb/GB1 "Premier League") clubs and, once again, they outspent any other league in the world - by some distance. Premier League clubs €2.33 billion on new players with star names like [Leny Yoro](https://www.transfermarkt.us/leny-yoro/profil/spieler/923831 "Leny Yoro"), [João Félix](https://www.transfermarkt.us/jo-o-f-lix/profil/spieler/462250 "João Félix") and [Riccardo Calafiori](https://www.transfermarkt.us/riccardo-calafiori/profil/spieler/502821 "Riccardo Calafiori") moving to the English top-light.

  
  

[Premier League clubs, however, also broke the all-time record for highest transfer income by any league in history with €1.62 bn recouped from player sales](https://www.transfermarkt.us/-euro-1-62bn-in-player-sales-premier-league-breaks-transfer-income-record/view/news/443392). [Manchester City](https://www.transfermarkt.us/manchester-city/startseite/verein/281 "Manchester City") made the highest transfer profit in the Premier League, while Brighton had the biggest net spend of any team in the world! [Chelsea](https://www.transfermarkt.us/chelsea-fc/startseite/verein/631 "Chelsea FC") were the biggest spenders again with €239m paid out on new arrivals. But where does this rank in terms of the highest total transfer fees paid by a Premier League club in one window? Let’s find out.

  

## The Premier League’s biggest spenders in one transfer window

  

Chelsea’s total spend of €239m this summer would only rank 9th for biggest outlays in one window in Premier League history. The Stamford Bridge club are constantly scrutinized for their spending but they also €198m in sales and their net spend of €40.5m was just the 24th highest in the word. Chelsea, however, have spent the three largest amounts in one window in Premier League history and they’ve all arrived since BlueCo - fronted by Todd Boehly - gained ownership.

  

![Image 20](https://tmssl.akamaized.net//images/foto/newsansicht/big-spenders-1725626740-147377.png?lm=1725626747)As the graphic above illustrates, Chelsea’s €464m spend in the summer of 2023 is a record for English clubs with [Moisés Caicedo's](https://www.transfermarkt.us/mois-s-caicedo/profil/spieler/687626 "Moisés Caicedo") €116m arrival from Brighton a club record. The only winter window that features in the top ten belongs to Chelsea in January 2023 when they spent €330m on the likes of [Enzo Fernandez](https://www.transfermarkt.us/enzo-fern-ndez/profil/spieler/648195 "Enzo Fernández") and [Mykhaylo Mudryk](https://www.transfermarkt.us/mykhaylo-mudryk/profil/spieler/537860 "Mykhaylo Mudryk"). Chelsea feature five times in the top ten with Manchester City twice and [Manchester United](https://www.transfermarkt.us/manchester-united/startseite/verein/985 "Manchester United"), [Arsenal](https://www.transfermarkt.us/arsenal-fc/startseite/verein/11 "Arsenal FC") and [Tottenham](https://www.transfermarkt.us/tottenham-hotspur/startseite/verein/148 "Tottenham Hotspur") are in once.

The **2015–16 Premier League** (known as the **[Barclays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays "Barclays") Premier League** for sponsorship reasons) was the 24th season of the [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League"), the top English professional league for [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") clubs, since its establishment in 1992, and the 117th season of top-flight English football overall. The season began on 8 August 2015, and was scheduled to conclude on 15 May 2016.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-6) However, the match between [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") and [Bournemouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Bournemouth "AFC Bournemouth") on the final day was postponed to 17 May 2016 due to a suspicious package found at [Old Trafford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Trafford "Old Trafford").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-7)

[Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") began the season as defending champions of the [2014–15 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League "2014–15 Premier League"). Bournemouth, [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C.") and [Norwich City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwich_City_F.C. "Norwich City F.C.") entered as the three promoted teams from the [2014–15 Football League Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Football_League_Championship "2014–15 Football League Championship").

[Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C."), managed by Italian [Claudio Ranieri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudio_Ranieri "Claudio Ranieri"), were crowned champions for the first time in their 132-year history (with two games to spare), becoming the 24th club to become [English football champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_English_football_champions "List of English football champions"), and the sixth club to win the Premier League.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-8) Many commentators consider this to be one of the greatest sporting shocks in history, especially when it is considered that Leicester spent a great deal of the previous season at the bottom of the table before rallying towards the season's end to finish 14th. At the beginning of the season, bookmakers had given Leicester City odds of 5000/1 to win the league. On 28 November 2015, Leicester striker [Jamie Vardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Vardy "Jamie Vardy") set a new record by scoring in 11 consecutive matches with his goal against [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C."), surpassing [Ruud van Nistelrooy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruud_van_Nistelrooy "Ruud van Nistelrooy")'s [Premier League record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League_records_and_statistics "Premier League records and statistics") of 10 straight games with a goal, which he set in 2003.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-9)[Aston Villa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aston_Villa_F.C. "Aston Villa F.C."), one of seven teams who had played in the Premier League since [its inaugural season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992%E2%80%9393_FA_Premier_League "1992–93 FA Premier League"), were relegated from the top flight in England for the first time since 1987.

This was the last season in which the league was sponsored by Barclays; effective [the following season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Premier_League "2016–17 Premier League") onwards, it would simply be known as the Premier League, with no sponsors attached.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-10)

## Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Summary")]

[Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C.") were the surprise of the season. Following their late escape from relegation in the previous season many pundits had predicted that they would be relegated,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-11) and bookmakers gave 5,000–1 odds on them winning the title.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-Supremacy-12) After the dismissal of manager [Nigel Pearson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Pearson "Nigel Pearson"), they began the new season with Italian [Claudio Ranieri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudio_Ranieri "Claudio Ranieri") in charge. Pearson had been known for his short temper with the press, while Ranieri has a reputation for good humour.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-pearson-13) The appointment was met with scepticism by pundits, including Leicester fan and former player [Gary Lineker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Lineker "Gary Lineker"), as Ranieri had recently been sacked from his previous post as manager of the [Greece national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece_national_football_team "Greece national football team") after suffering [a humiliating defeat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Faroe_Islands_v_Greece_football_matches#2014_match "2014–15 Faroe Islands v Greece football matches") to the [Faroe Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faroe_Islands_national_football_team "Faroe Islands national football team") in his last game in charge.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-pearson-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-14)

Despite winning their opening game against [Sunderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunderland_A.F.C. "Sunderland A.F.C.") and topping the table, they dropped back following a 5–2 home defeat to [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.") in September.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-compare-15) However, aided by [Jamie Vardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Vardy "Jamie Vardy")'s record feat of scoring in eleven consecutive Premier League games,[[i]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-17) they then remained unbeaten – and returned to the top of the table – until 26 December, when a 1–0 defeat to [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") dropped them to second place. They returned to the top after a 1–1 draw with [Aston Villa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aston_Villa_F.C. "Aston Villa F.C.") on 16 January, and remained there for the rest of the season.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-compare-15) Following a 2–2 draw between [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") and [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") at [Stamford Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamford_Bridge_(stadium) "Stamford Bridge (stadium)") on 2 May 2016, and having two more games to play, Leicester City were confirmed champions, their first title in the top flight of English football, eclipsing the runners-up spot they reached in 1929.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-Supremacy-12)

Defending champions Chelsea sacked manager [José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho") in December while in 16th place and eventually failed to qualify for European football for the first time in two decades. [Eden Hazard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Hazard "Eden Hazard"), the previous season's [PFA Players' Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFA_Players'_Player_of_the_Year "PFA Players' Player of the Year"), did not score a league goal until late April.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-18) They eventually finished 10th, breaking the record for lowest finish for a Premier League title holder – 7th, held jointly by [Blackburn Rovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackburn_Rovers_F.C. "Blackburn Rovers F.C.") in [1995–96](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995%E2%80%9396_FA_Premier_League "1995–96 FA Premier League") and [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") in [2013–14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Premier_League "2013–14 Premier League").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-19) This record only stood for one year, as Leicester City finished 12th the [following season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Premier_League "2016–17 Premier League").

Arsenal, looking for their first title since 2004 and following a poor start, improved and in early January took the top spot from Leicester. However, a poor run of results, including draws with Liverpool,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-20)[Stoke City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_City_F.C. "Stoke City F.C.")[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-21) and [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C."),[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-22) and a loss to Chelsea[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-23) saw them drop to fourth by mid-February. They remained in contention, but draws with [West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C."), Sunderland and Crystal Palace in April saw their title hopes vanish.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-24)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-26)

Meanwhile, Arsenal's London rivals Tottenham Hotspur won six matches in a row, and when Arsenal lost to Manchester United at the end of February, Tottenham leapfrogged them into second place,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-27) where they remained until the final weekend of the season. Draws with [West Bromwich Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bromwich_Albion_F.C. "West Bromwich Albion F.C.")[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-28) and Chelsea—in a game now known as the ‘[Battle of the Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C.%E2%80%93Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C._rivalry#2016:_'Battle_of_the_Bridge' "Chelsea F.C.–Tottenham Hotspur F.C. rivalry")’—prevented them from winning their first league title since 1961.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-29) After a 2–1 home loss to Southampton and a 5–1 defeat away to [Newcastle United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newcastle_United_F.C. "Newcastle United F.C.") in their final two matches, Tottenham ended the season in third place, one point behind Arsenal.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-30)

[West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C."), in their final season at the [Boleyn Ground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boleyn_Ground "Boleyn Ground") after 112 years, achieved 62 points, a club record for a Premier League campaign. It was also the first Premier League season where they had finished with a positive goal difference (+14) and West Ham's eight defeats was also a club record for the fewest losses suffered in a Premier League season.

Aston Villa, a presence in the Premier League since the league's foundation in 1992 and present in the top division since the 1988–89 season, were the first team to be relegated, after a 1–0 loss at Manchester United on 16 April.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-31) On 11 May, Sunderland won 3–0 against [Everton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everton_F.C. "Everton F.C."), a result which relegated both Newcastle United and [Norwich City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwich_City_F.C. "Norwich City F.C.") with one game remaining.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-32)

All the final fixtures of the season were scheduled for 15 May and were to kick off at the same time. However, Manchester United's home game against [Bournemouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Bournemouth "AFC Bournemouth") was called off after [Old Trafford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Trafford "Old Trafford") was evacuated because of the discovery of a suspicious device, which was destroyed in a controlled explosion. It was confirmed to be an accidental leftover from a training exercise.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-33) The match was played two days later on 17 May, with United winning 3–1.

### Reactions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Reactions")]

The unlikely nature of Leicester's title led to a flood of coverage from across the globe. Prime Minister [David Cameron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Cameron "David Cameron") tweeted his congratulations, saying it was "An extraordinary, thoroughly deserved, Premier League title". Congratulations were also sent by the Italian Prime Minister [Matteo Renzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matteo_Renzi "Matteo Renzi"), who praised his compatriot Ranieri.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-world-34)

Premier League chief executive [Richard Scudamore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Scudamore "Richard Scudamore") called it "probably the biggest sporting story ever".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-35) Former Leicester manager [Martin O'Neill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_O'Neill "Martin O'Neill") described it as the "greatest achievement, obviously, of this century".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-36)[Gary Lineker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Lineker "Gary Lineker"), the former Leicester striker who led a consortium that saved the club from administration in 2002, had said he would host the BBC football show _[Match of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Match\_of\_the\_Day "Match of the Day")_ in his underwear if Leicester won the title. After they won the title, he did indeed present the show clad only in boxer shorts.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-37)[[ii]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-39) He said: "There were no odds that I would have taken at the start of the season. No odds. You could have given me 10 million to one and I'd have said 'Nah, it's a waste of a quid'".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-40)[José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho"), manager of 2015 champions Chelsea and Ranieri's replacement at the same team eleven years earlier, sent his congratulations, saying: "I lost my title to Claudio Ranieri and it is with incredible emotion that I live this magic moment in his career."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-Ranieriquote-41) Ranieri said, after winning his first title at the age of 64, that he would not have appreciated it as a young man: "Now I am an old man I can feel it much better."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-Ranieriquote-41)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-42)

The long odds that bookmakers had given at the start of the season on victory for Leicester led to them incurring losses of up to £25 million, with one punter winning over £100,000, having wagered £20 at the original 5,000–1 odds;[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-43) the largest payout was £200,000 to an anonymous bettor who wagered £100 on the team in October when the odds had gone down to 2,000–1.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-44)

Superstitious claims of phenomena helping Leicester win the league include the club's Thai owners engaging Buddhist monks to bless the players,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-world-34) and the [reburial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exhumation_and_reburial_of_Richard_III_of_England "Exhumation and reburial of Richard III of England") of King [Richard III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_III_of_England "Richard III of England") in [the city's cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_Cathedral "Leicester Cathedral") in March 2015.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-45)

## Teams

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Teams")]

Twenty teams competed in the league– the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Football_League_Championship "2014–15 Football League Championship"). The promoted teams were [Bournemouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Bournemouth "AFC Bournemouth") (playing in the top flight for the first time ever), [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C.") (returning to the top flight after eight years) and [Norwich City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwich_City_F.C. "Norwich City F.C.") (returning after a season's absence). They replaced [Hull City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hull_City_A.F.C. "Hull City A.F.C.") (relegated to the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Football_League_Championship "2015–16 Football League Championship") after a two-year spell in the top flight), [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") and [Queens Park Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_Park_Rangers_F.C. "Queens Park Rangers F.C.") (both teams relegated after a season's presence).

The **2015–16 Premier League** (known as the **[Barclays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays "Barclays") Premier League** for sponsorship reasons) was the 24th season of the [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League"), the top English professional league for [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") clubs, since its establishment in 1992, and the 117th season of top-flight English football overall. The season began on 8 August 2015, and was scheduled to conclude on 15 May 2016.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-6) However, the match between [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") and [Bournemouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Bournemouth "AFC Bournemouth") on the final day was postponed to 17 May 2016 due to a suspicious package found at [Old Trafford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Trafford "Old Trafford").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-7)

[Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") began the season as defending champions of the [2014–15 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League "2014–15 Premier League"). Bournemouth, [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C.") and [Norwich City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwich_City_F.C. "Norwich City F.C.") entered as the three promoted teams from the [2014–15 Football League Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Football_League_Championship "2014–15 Football League Championship").

[Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C."), managed by Italian [Claudio Ranieri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudio_Ranieri "Claudio Ranieri"), were crowned champions for the first time in their 132-year history (with two games to spare), becoming the 24th club to become [English football champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_English_football_champions "List of English football champions"), and the sixth club to win the Premier League.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-8) Many commentators consider this to be one of the greatest sporting shocks in history, especially when it is considered that Leicester spent a great deal of the previous season at the bottom of the table before rallying towards the season's end to finish 14th. At the beginning of the season, bookmakers had given Leicester City odds of 5000/1 to win the league. On 28 November 2015, Leicester striker [Jamie Vardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Vardy "Jamie Vardy") set a new record by scoring in 11 consecutive matches with his goal against [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C."), surpassing [Ruud van Nistelrooy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruud_van_Nistelrooy "Ruud van Nistelrooy")'s [Premier League record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League_records_and_statistics "Premier League records and statistics") of 10 straight games with a goal, which he set in 2003.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-9)[Aston Villa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aston_Villa_F.C. "Aston Villa F.C."), one of seven teams who had played in the Premier League since [its inaugural season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992%E2%80%9393_FA_Premier_League "1992–93 FA Premier League"), were relegated from the top flight in England for the first time since 1987.

This was the last season in which the league was sponsored by Barclays; effective [the following season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Premier_League "2016–17 Premier League") onwards, it would simply be known as the Premier League, with no sponsors attached.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-10)

## Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Summary")]

[Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C.") were the surprise of the season. Following their late escape from relegation in the previous season many pundits had predicted that they would be relegated,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-11) and bookmakers gave 5,000–1 odds on them winning the title.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-Supremacy-12) After the dismissal of manager [Nigel Pearson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Pearson "Nigel Pearson"), they began the new season with Italian [Claudio Ranieri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudio_Ranieri "Claudio Ranieri") in charge. Pearson had been known for his short temper with the press, while Ranieri has a reputation for good humour.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-pearson-13) The appointment was met with scepticism by pundits, including Leicester fan and former player [Gary Lineker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Lineker "Gary Lineker"), as Ranieri had recently been sacked from his previous post as manager of the [Greece national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece_national_football_team "Greece national football team") after suffering [a humiliating defeat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Faroe_Islands_v_Greece_football_matches#2014_match "2014–15 Faroe Islands v Greece football matches") to the [Faroe Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faroe_Islands_national_football_team "Faroe Islands national football team") in his last game in charge.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-pearson-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-14)

Despite winning their opening game against [Sunderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunderland_A.F.C. "Sunderland A.F.C.") and topping the table, they dropped back following a 5–2 home defeat to [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.") in September.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-compare-15) However, aided by [Jamie Vardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Vardy "Jamie Vardy")'s record feat of scoring in eleven consecutive Premier League games,[[i]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-17) they then remained unbeaten – and returned to the top of the table – until 26 December, when a 1–0 defeat to [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") dropped them to second place. They returned to the top after a 1–1 draw with [Aston Villa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aston_Villa_F.C. "Aston Villa F.C.") on 16 January, and remained there for the rest of the season.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-compare-15) Following a 2–2 draw between [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") and [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") at [Stamford Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamford_Bridge_(stadium) "Stamford Bridge (stadium)") on 2 May 2016, and having two more games to play, Leicester City were confirmed champions, their first title in the top flight of English football, eclipsing the runners-up spot they reached in 1929.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-Supremacy-12)

Defending champions Chelsea sacked manager [José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho") in December while in 16th place and eventually failed to qualify for European football for the first time in two decades. [Eden Hazard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Hazard "Eden Hazard"), the previous season's [PFA Players' Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFA_Players'_Player_of_the_Year "PFA Players' Player of the Year"), did not score a league goal until late April.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-18) They eventually finished 10th, breaking the record for lowest finish for a Premier League title holder – 7th, held jointly by [Blackburn Rovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackburn_Rovers_F.C. "Blackburn Rovers F.C.") in [1995–96](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995%E2%80%9396_FA_Premier_League "1995–96 FA Premier League") and [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") in [2013–14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Premier_League "2013–14 Premier League").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-19) This record only stood for one year, as Leicester City finished 12th the [following season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Premier_League "2016–17 Premier League").

Arsenal, looking for their first title since 2004 and following a poor start, improved and in early January took the top spot from Leicester. However, a poor run of results, including draws with Liverpool,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-20)[Stoke City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_City_F.C. "Stoke City F.C.")[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-21) and [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C."),[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-22) and a loss to Chelsea[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-23) saw them drop to fourth by mid-February. They remained in contention, but draws with [West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C."), Sunderland and Crystal Palace in April saw their title hopes vanish.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-24)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-26)

Meanwhile, Arsenal's London rivals Tottenham Hotspur won six matches in a row, and when Arsenal lost to Manchester United at the end of February, Tottenham leapfrogged them into second place,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-27) where they remained until the final weekend of the season. Draws with [West Bromwich Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bromwich_Albion_F.C. "West Bromwich Albion F.C.")[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-28) and Chelsea—in a game now known as the ‘[Battle of the Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C.%E2%80%93Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C._rivalry#2016:_'Battle_of_the_Bridge' "Chelsea F.C.–Tottenham Hotspur F.C. rivalry")’—prevented them from winning their first league title since 1961.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-29) After a 2–1 home loss to Southampton and a 5–1 defeat away to [Newcastle United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newcastle_United_F.C. "Newcastle United F.C.") in their final two matches, Tottenham ended the season in third place, one point behind Arsenal.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-30)

[West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C."), in their final season at the [Boleyn Ground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boleyn_Ground "Boleyn Ground") after 112 years, achieved 62 points, a club record for a Premier League campaign. It was also the first Premier League season where they had finished with a positive goal difference (+14) and West Ham's eight defeats was also a club record for the fewest losses suffered in a Premier League season.

Aston Villa, a presence in the Premier League since the league's foundation in 1992 and present in the top division since the 1988–89 season, were the first team to be relegated, after a 1–0 loss at Manchester United on 16 April.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-31) On 11 May, Sunderland won 3–0 against [Everton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everton_F.C. "Everton F.C."), a result which relegated both Newcastle United and [Norwich City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwich_City_F.C. "Norwich City F.C.") with one game remaining.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-32)

All the final fixtures of the season were scheduled for 15 May and were to kick off at the same time. However, Manchester United's home game against [Bournemouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Bournemouth "AFC Bournemouth") was called off after [Old Trafford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Trafford "Old Trafford") was evacuated because of the discovery of a suspicious device, which was destroyed in a controlled explosion. It was confirmed to be an accidental leftover from a training exercise.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-33) The match was played two days later on 17 May, with United winning 3–1.

### Reactions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Reactions")]

The unlikely nature of Leicester's title led to a flood of coverage from across the globe. Prime Minister [David Cameron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Cameron "David Cameron") tweeted his congratulations, saying it was "An extraordinary, thoroughly deserved, Premier League title". Congratulations were also sent by the Italian Prime Minister [Matteo Renzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matteo_Renzi "Matteo Renzi"), who praised his compatriot Ranieri.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-world-34)

Premier League chief executive [Richard Scudamore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Scudamore "Richard Scudamore") called it "probably the biggest sporting story ever".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-35) Former Leicester manager [Martin O'Neill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_O'Neill "Martin O'Neill") described it as the "greatest achievement, obviously, of this century".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-36)[Gary Lineker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Lineker "Gary Lineker"), the former Leicester striker who led a consortium that saved the club from administration in 2002, had said he would host the BBC football show _[Match of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Match\_of\_the\_Day "Match of the Day")_ in his underwear if Leicester won the title. After they won the title, he did indeed present the show clad only in boxer shorts.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-37)[[ii]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-39) He said: "There were no odds that I would have taken at the start of the season. No odds. You could have given me 10 million to one and I'd have said 'Nah, it's a waste of a quid'".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-40)[José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho"), manager of 2015 champions Chelsea and Ranieri's replacement at the same team eleven years earlier, sent his congratulations, saying: "I lost my title to Claudio Ranieri and it is with incredible emotion that I live this magic moment in his career."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-Ranieriquote-41) Ranieri said, after winning his first title at the age of 64, that he would not have appreciated it as a young man: "Now I am an old man I can feel it much better."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-Ranieriquote-41)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-42)

The long odds that bookmakers had given at the start of the season on victory for Leicester led to them incurring losses of up to £25 million, with one punter winning over £100,000, having wagered £20 at the original 5,000–1 odds;[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-43) the largest payout was £200,000 to an anonymous bettor who wagered £100 on the team in October when the odds had gone down to 2,000–1.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-44)

Superstitious claims of phenomena helping Leicester win the league include the club's Thai owners engaging Buddhist monks to bless the players,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-world-34) and the [reburial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exhumation_and_reburial_of_Richard_III_of_England "Exhumation and reburial of Richard III of England") of King [Richard III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_III_of_England "Richard III of England") in [the city's cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_Cathedral "Leicester Cathedral") in March 2015.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League#cite_note-45)

## Teams

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Teams")]

Twenty teams competed in the league– the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Football_League_Championship "2014–15 Football League Championship"). The promoted teams were [Bournemouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Bournemouth "AFC Bournemouth") (playing in the top flight for the first time ever), [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C.") (returning to the top flight after eight years) and [Norwich City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwich_City_F.C. "Norwich City F.C.") (returning after a season's absence). They replaced [Hull City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hull_City_A.F.C. "Hull City A.F.C.") (relegated to the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Football_League_Championship "2015–16 Football League Championship") after a two-year spell in the top flight), [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") and [Queens Park Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_Park_Rangers_F.C. "Queens Park Rangers F.C.") (both teams relegated after a season's presence).

The **2014–15 Premier League** (known as the **[Barclays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays "Barclays") Premier League** for sponsorship reasons) was the 23rd season of the [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League"), the top English professional league for association football clubs, since its establishment in 1992, and the 116th season of top-flight English football overall. The fixtures were announced on 18 June 2014.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-5) The season started on 16 August 2014 and concluded on 24 May 2015.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-6)

[Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") came into the season as defending champions of the [2013–14 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Premier_League "2013–14 Premier League"). [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C."), [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") and [Queens Park Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_Park_Rangers_F.C. "Queens Park Rangers F.C.") entered as the three promoted teams.

On 3 May 2015, [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") won the title with three games to spare after a 1–0 home win over [Crystal Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal_Palace_F.C. "Crystal Palace F.C.").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-7) It was their first league title since 2010, their fourth Premier League title and their fifth English league title overall.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-8) Holders Manchester City eventually finished second, after a short drop to fourth a few weeks before the final match.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-9)

[Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") were the first team to be relegated on 9 May 2015 despite beating [Hull City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hull_City_A.F.C. "Hull City A.F.C.") 1–0, while [Queens Park Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_Park_Rangers_F.C. "Queens Park Rangers F.C.") suffered the same fate after a 6–0 demolition by Manchester City the next day.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-11) Hull City were the third and final team to be relegated after [Newcastle United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newcastle_United_F.C. "Newcastle United F.C.") beat [West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C.") 2–0.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-15) They drew 0–0 against [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") on the final day of the season.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-16)

Manchester City's [Sergio Agüero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Ag%C3%BCero "Sergio Agüero") won the Golden Boot with 26 goals, with his teammate [Joe Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Hart "Joe Hart") clinching a record fourth Golden Glove, having kept 14 clean sheets.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-18)[Eden Hazard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Hazard "Eden Hazard") and [José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho") were named as Player and Manager of the Season respectively.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-AnnualAwards-19)

## Teams

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Teams")]

Twenty teams competed in the league – the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Football_League_Championship "2013–14 Football League Championship"). The promoted teams were [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C."), [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.")[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-20) and [Queens Park Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_Park_Rangers_F.C. "Queens Park Rangers F.C."), returning to the top flight after respective absences of ten years, four years and one year. They replaced [Norwich City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwich_City_F.C. "Norwich City F.C."), [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C.") and [Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C."), who were relegated to the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Football_League_Championship "2014–15 Football League Championship") after their respective top-flight spells of three years, thirteen years and one year.

## Results

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Results")]

On 3 May 2015, Chelsea beat Crystal Palace 1–0 to secure the Premier League title with three games to play. [PFA Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFA_Player_of_the_Year "PFA Player of the Year") winner [Eden Hazard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Hazard "Eden Hazard") scored the winning goal near the end of the first half, heading in the rebound of his own penalty kick. The win left Chelsea 16 points ahead of Arsenal, which had five games remaining.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-CBC-84) Chelsea were atop the standings the entire year, having got off to a good start.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-CBC-84)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-85) For Chelsea, it was the fourth title in the last eleven years, but first in the last six seasons. It was the fifth title in the club's 110-year history. "We showed absolutely everything since day one, everything football demands from a team," said manager [José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho"). "We had fantastic attacking football, we had fantastic domination ... we defended amazingly well."[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-CBC-84) It was Mourinho's 22nd career title. He won titles at Chelsea in 2005 and 2006, before being forced out by owner [Roman Abramovich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Abramovich "Roman Abramovich"), and returning in 2013. [Diego Costa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Costa "Diego Costa") led Chelsea with 20 goals.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-CBC-84)

The **2014–15 Premier League** (known as the **[Barclays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays "Barclays") Premier League** for sponsorship reasons) was the 23rd season of the [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League"), the top English professional league for association football clubs, since its establishment in 1992, and the 116th season of top-flight English football overall. The fixtures were announced on 18 June 2014.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-5) The season started on 16 August 2014 and concluded on 24 May 2015.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-6)

[Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") came into the season as defending champions of the [2013–14 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Premier_League "2013–14 Premier League"). [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C."), [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") and [Queens Park Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_Park_Rangers_F.C. "Queens Park Rangers F.C.") entered as the three promoted teams.

On 3 May 2015, [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") won the title with three games to spare after a 1–0 home win over [Crystal Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal_Palace_F.C. "Crystal Palace F.C.").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-7) It was their first league title since 2010, their fourth Premier League title and their fifth English league title overall.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-8) Holders Manchester City eventually finished second, after a short drop to fourth a few weeks before the final match.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-9)

[Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") were the first team to be relegated on 9 May 2015 despite beating [Hull City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hull_City_A.F.C. "Hull City A.F.C.") 1–0, while [Queens Park Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_Park_Rangers_F.C. "Queens Park Rangers F.C.") suffered the same fate after a 6–0 demolition by Manchester City the next day.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-11) Hull City were the third and final team to be relegated after [Newcastle United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newcastle_United_F.C. "Newcastle United F.C.") beat [West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C.") 2–0.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-15) They drew 0–0 against [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") on the final day of the season.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-16)

Manchester City's [Sergio Agüero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Ag%C3%BCero "Sergio Agüero") won the Golden Boot with 26 goals, with his teammate [Joe Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Hart "Joe Hart") clinching a record fourth Golden Glove, having kept 14 clean sheets.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-18)[Eden Hazard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Hazard "Eden Hazard") and [José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho") were named as Player and Manager of the Season respectively.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-AnnualAwards-19)

## Teams

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Teams")]

Twenty teams competed in the league – the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Football_League_Championship "2013–14 Football League Championship"). The promoted teams were [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C."), [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.")[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-20) and [Queens Park Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_Park_Rangers_F.C. "Queens Park Rangers F.C."), returning to the top flight after respective absences of ten years, four years and one year. They replaced [Norwich City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwich_City_F.C. "Norwich City F.C."), [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C.") and [Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C."), who were relegated to the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Football_League_Championship "2014–15 Football League Championship") after their respective top-flight spells of three years, thirteen years and one year.

## Results

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Results")]

On 3 May 2015, Chelsea beat Crystal Palace 1–0 to secure the Premier League title with three games to play. [PFA Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFA_Player_of_the_Year "PFA Player of the Year") winner [Eden Hazard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Hazard "Eden Hazard") scored the winning goal near the end of the first half, heading in the rebound of his own penalty kick. The win left Chelsea 16 points ahead of Arsenal, which had five games remaining.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-CBC-84) Chelsea were atop the standings the entire year, having got off to a good start.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-CBC-84)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-85) For Chelsea, it was the fourth title in the last eleven years, but first in the last six seasons. It was the fifth title in the club's 110-year history. "We showed absolutely everything since day one, everything football demands from a team," said manager [José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho"). "We had fantastic attacking football, we had fantastic domination ... we defended amazingly well."[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-CBC-84) It was Mourinho's 22nd career title. He won titles at Chelsea in 2005 and 2006, before being forced out by owner [Roman Abramovich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Abramovich "Roman Abramovich"), and returning in 2013. [Diego Costa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Costa "Diego Costa") led Chelsea with 20 goals.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League#cite_note-CBC-84)
